newsitem.title: USA: Rubin voices optimism on U.S. exports.
newsitem.headline: Rubin voices optimism on U.S. exports.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin Friday voiced optimism about U.S. exports, saying U.S. industries are competitive.

Speaking to reporters before a speech to the Bretton Woods Committee, Rubin also reiterated the Clinton administration's opposition to a balanced budget amendment to the constitution, calling it "unwise" and "dangerous."
Rubin played down recent signs that U.S. export growth may be stalling out, saying that exports vary from month to month and that special factors could have been at play in their recent performance.
"I remain very optimistic about exports going forward," he said.
He said that exports have been on the rise under President Clinton because of the competitiveness of U.S. industry and the success of the administration in opening up foreign markets.
"The U.S. is competitive for probably the first time in 15 or 20 years across a broad array of industries," he said.
Turning to the domestic scene, Rubin denied that Clinton had flip-flopped on the issue of a balanced budget amendment and insisted that the President remained opposed to such a measure.
"His opposition is unchanged," the treasury chief said.
While Clinton is "very strongly" in favor of balancing the budget, a constitutional amendment would create a "rigidity that could be dangerous," Rubin added.
